review_candidates.title: Project Director
review_candidates.description: Right across infrastructure, there’s a requirement to not only maintain, but also renew and reimagine. Whatever stage you’re at in your career; with us you’ll have an opportunity to grow and develop. Delivering essential infrastructure services for life, while being safety first, and client and customer centric in a friendly, fun and respectful environment where you are encouraged to thrive. Where you’ll be working? BGEN is one of the UK's largest multidisciplinary design and build contractors with over 100 years of industry experience. We support clients in the Water, Power & Energy, Pharmaceutical, Nuclear and Food and Beverage industries to deliver next generation, value-added engineering solutions. What you'll be doing? The Project Director is accountable for the safe, successful, and profitable delivery of major projects from tender handover through execution, commissioning, and close-out. The role provides strategic leadership to multidisciplinary teams, ensuring projects are delivered in line with contractual, commercial, programme, quality, safety, and operational objectives while maintaining strong client relationships and governance standards. Key responsibilities include leading project teams, promoting a high-performance culture, and ensuring effective mobilisation, execution, and completion of projects. The Project Director owns overall health, safety, environmental, and wellbeing performance, manages project profitability, cash flow, commercial strategy, contractual matters, and risk management. They oversee programme controls, project reporting, engineering governance, quality assurance, and commissioning activities. Acting as the senior representative to clients and stakeholders, the Project Director leads governance reviews, manages strategic relationships, and protects the organisation’s reputation. The role is ultimately accountable for safety, programme delivery, financial performance, quality, client satisfaction, workforce leadership, governance compliance, and achieving the project's strategic objectives. You will bring: You are an accomplished Project Director with extensive experience delivering major E&I and Mechanical projects from concept through commissioning and handover. You combine strong technical credibility with commercial awareness, strategic leadership, and a relentless focus on safety, quality, programme, and client satisfaction. You are comfortable operating in complex, high-value environments and have the capability to lead large multidisciplinary teams to deliver exceptional project outcomes while protecting commercial performance and strengthening long-term client relationships. Demonstrable experience leading the successful delivery of large, complex Electrical, Instrumentation and Mechanical (E&I/M) projects within highly regulated industries such as Nuclear, Power, Energy, Water, Pharmaceutical, or Industrial Manufacturing. Proven track record of providing strategic leadership across multidisciplinary project teams, including engineering, construction, quality, commissioning, commercial, planning, and project controls functions. Strong understanding of E&I and mechanical installation, testing, commissioning, construction methodologies, and engineering assurance processes, with the ability to challenge and support technical decisions at a senior level. Significant experience managing major project budgets, cash flow, profitability, risk, change control, and contractual obligations under NEC, FIDIC, or similar forms of contract. An exceptional safety leadership record with a visible commitment to Health, Safety, Environmental and Wellbeing performance, fostering a culture where safety is the first priority and everyone takes responsibility. Strong commercial and contractual acumen, with experience managing client relationships, claims, variations, dispute avoidance, and negotiation of complex project matters. Experience establishing robust project governance, reporting, programme controls, risk management, and performance management frameworks to ensure successful project outcomes. Proven ability to build and lead high-performing teams, developing future leaders and creating a culture of accountability, collaboration, inclusion, and continuous improvement. Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently with clients, regulators, supply chain partners, senior executives, and project teams. What’s in it for you? We offer a range of benefits designed to support your life in and out of work, some of which include; Company Pension Scheme Death in Service Benefit Opportunity to purchase additional holidays per year (up to 5 days for full time employees) My Rewards - offering discounts on high street and online shopping Employee assistance programme 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Car Allowance/ Salary Sacrifice scheme In addition, this role offers; Private health care for you Recommend a friend - get rewarded for introducing people to us! About Us We want to be an employer of choice and a great place to work, attracting diverse and talented people, who join us and make a difference. We’re one of the Top 100 UK companies actively supporting and recruiting veterans. Our ENABLE inclusion networks bring together people who have a shared passion, to help create an environment where everyone belongs. Our values help to shape our culture and how we work with one another. We recruit with these values in mind, to ensure your aspirations, and ways of working, align with ours. We’re responsible and go further for our people, clients, communities and the planet We’re open and seek new and better ways of exceeding expectations We’re together and as one team; the whole is greater than the sum of the parts We’re ambitious and embrace opportunity, to lead essential infrastructure services for life Whether you’re a trainee, apprentice or graduate, or progressing through your career, our people benefit from industry recognised programmes, training and development. It’s an exceptional time to be a part of M Group. Please note: Occasionally, job adverts might be closed before the stated closing date. Do apply as soon as possible to ensure your application is considered. For certain roles, successful candidates will be subject to 3rd party background checks as part of the hiring process. review_candidates.title: Platform engineer
review_candidates.description: Hybrid with travel to Bath, London and Edinburgh a couple times a month About Us Seccl is the Octopus-owned embedded investment platform, on a mission to help more people invest, and invest well. We’re building the infrastructure behind the next generation of investing. Our technology already powers some of the UK’s most ambitious fintechs, banks, financial advisers and wealth firms, with close to a million investors relying on Seccl-powered platforms. And we’re now expanding into Europe. We’ve got a proven product, strong momentum and big ambitions for what comes next: helping more household-name brands launch and scale investment propositions, entering new markets and replacing outdated investment infrastructure with technology that’s faster, simpler and built for scale. We’re proud to be part of Octopus, one of the UK’s most successful privately held investment and technology groups. That gives us the backing and long-term perspective to build something substantial, while keeping the pace and energy of a high-growth business. Seccl and Octopus are both B Corp certified and share a belief that profit and purpose should go hand in hand. If you want to help shape the future of investing in the UK and across Europe, you’ll be in good company. Check out the Seccl website to see what we’re building and read more about our mission to shape the future of investments. The role We're looking for a Platform engineer to shape and evolve the platform that underpins our investment products. You’ll be someone who loves understanding engineering problems and enabling teams to self-serve their needs. You view the cloud platform as a product, and engineering as your customer. The role is within our Cloud Resilience team - a critical squad within our engineering organisation responsible for empowering squads to build and run their own services. We’re primarily in AWS , utilising Lambda, ECS, SQS, EventBridge, API Gateway, Aurora, Redshift among others. Our main data store is MongoDB Atlas and our observability platform is Datadog . Our application is written in Typescript/NodeJS and our infrastructure is defined in Terraform . On a typical day you will be… Architecting, implementing, and maintaining scalable, secure infrastructure in AWS using Terraform. Designing cloud-native solutions using MongoDB, Lambda, API Gateway, and other AWS services with a strong focus on serverless. Contributing to incident response efforts, production readiness, and reliability initiatives across engineering squads. Enhancing observability and platform insight through actionable alerting and data visibility using Datadog. Continuously improving CI/CD processes with GitHub Actions, reducing friction in delivery pipelines. Collaborating with software engineers (working in Node.js/TypeScript) to ensure secure, performant, and resilient applications. Mentoring engineers and champion DevOps culture and best practices across teams. This role’s for you if... You’re a pragmatic platform engineer with experience in regulated environments, balancing delivery with compliance and operational excellence. You’re confident working with JavaScript/TypeScript-based applications and collaborating closely with development teams. You know what “good” looks like for databases like MongoDB and Postgres and can diagnose, design, and optimise for scale and resilience. You care deeply about observability - you don’t just monitor systems, you build alerts that engineers can act on. You’re fluent in AWS best practices, infrastructure-as-code (Terraform), and CI/CD tooling like GitHub Actions. You’ve had exposure to architectural decisions and willingness to own of platform-level outcomes. This role isn’t for you if... You rely on a lot of top-down direction. Here, you’ll have a lot of freedom and ownership of your role, and you’ll be expected to shape your own progression You’re not comfortable working in a fast-paced environment. Our speed and scalability are what set us apart; you need to be able to act quickly and think on your feet You struggle to follow through on ideas. We value people who do what they say they will. If you care about something, you have the freedom here to make it happen You don’t like change. You’ll get on great here if you relish the ambiguity of rapid growth and are willing to embrace uncertainty What’s In It For You… We offer a generous mix of benefits for the things that really matter to our people, including: 💰 A salary between £55,000 and £75,000 – dependant on experience + reviewed annually 🌴 27 days holiday + bank holidays (some can be flexible) + day off on your birthday + three days (full time) per year for Dependant leave 💙 Two volunteering days per year 🌎 Option to work abroad for up to six weeks a year 🌟 Secclbrate - our recognition programme that offers a mix of flexible rewards including extra pay, additional holiday and increased learning budget 🏅 Length of service award – one month paid sabbatical at eight years ✅ 6% employer pension contribution, and life assurance 🏥 Private medical insurance with AXA Health 👪 Enhanced Parental leave 💻 MacBook and up to £500 home office set up budget 📖 £750 per person learning budget 🌻 Health and wellbeing initiatives including free therapy via Wellness Cloud, mental health support via Headspace 🌱 Strong financial wellbeing focus including access to Octopus Money, Octopus Share Incentive Plan and will writing offering via Octopus Legacy 🎁 Perkbox – Flexi-points giving you a range of discounts and perks including free weekly coffee, gym and retail discounts 🚲 Access to initiatives like Cycle to Work and Octopus Electric Vehicle Leasing Our culture We're proud to put people first, creating a culture where we truly listen to what matters most to them. Our transparent and inclusive environment encourages diversity of thought, challenge and experimentation. Check out our Glassdoor page for the latest reviews or our LinkedIn for company updates and insights from the team. Interview process Interviewing Is a Two-way Thing, And We Want You To Have The Time And Opportunity To Get To Know Us, As Much As We Are Getting To Know You. Our Interviews Are Conversational, So Come With Questions And Be Curious. In General, You Can Expect The Interview Process To Look a Bit Like This, (following An Initial Chat With One Of Our Talent Team) First stage – 60 mins Cloud System Design interview Second stage – 60 mins Terraform Code Review Interview Final stage – 45 mins bar-raiser culture-based interview ⏳ We’ll only close this role once we have enough applications for the next stage. Please submit your application as soon as possible to make sure you don’t miss out and you should expect to hear back from us within one to two weeks of applying. 🌈 Our aim is to build a diverse and inclusive company of awesome people, with unique skills, passions and experiences. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to age, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, or veteran, neurodiversity or disability status. If this sounds like your kind of thing, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t tick every box. We’d love to hear from you! Compensation Range: £55K - £75K

review_candidates.title: Platform Engineer - SKA-Low Telescope
review_candidates.description: Acknowledgement of Country CSIRO acknowledges the Traditional Owners of the land, sea and waters, of the area that we live and work on across Australia. We acknowledge their continuing connection to their culture and pay our respects to their Elders past and present. View our vision towards reconciliation . Role highlights Great ongoing opportunity to build computing platforms for a global science project Apply your platform expertise in a unique environment Join a diverse team powering one of the world’s largest telescopes! About CSIRO As Australia's national science agency, CSIRO is solving the greatest challenges through innovative science and technology. Many of our iconic innovations were once considered impossible until someone, just like you, joined us and took on the challenge. Visit CSIRO.au for more information. The opportunity The SKA-Low project is part of the SKA Observatory’s global mission to build the world’s largest and most advanced radio telescope. In Australia, SKA-Low is being developed on Wajarri Yamaji Country in remote Western Australia, combining high-performance computing, advanced networking and cutting-edge software systems to process vast volumes of scientific data. This is a unique opportunity to contribute to a globally significant, next-generation scientific infrastructure.
